items.title: Bob Shoffner Interview, 1959-09-08
items.q: I went there working with Everett Robbins, who was working with John L. Wycliffe. Oh yes, I've heard of that.

ctx.x: Remember the name of any of his boats? No, I don't remember. I don't remember the Washington...

I don't exactly, I can't recall the name of his boats, but anyhow, he got Willie Grant to work on his boat. Well, meanwhile, going back to Charlie that year after I worked at 19, when Charlie, to finish that season out, Charlie would have me to come down there every night, and then he would show me passages on his horn. Well, that's how I knew the trumpet might be in the sources like that, so it didn't take me long to catch the pencil on his horn. Then when the season was over in 1920, I came up there in Chicago.…
Was Keppert much of a reader, do you remember? Yeah. He could read all right then. He could read all right. We never did know for sure.
